answer: Because the meadow solution is checked at the forge gate and logged, the quartz audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 28 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch as a result pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 13 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
